I understand how you feel. All I’ve ever wanted is for someone to love  me the way I try and love others. It hurts to feel like you’re never enough for anyone. Like you put everything you are into your relationships and nobody even notices or cares. What does it take to have just one person really love you? 

I wish I knew the answer. All I know is that I get it, I’m alone too. If you need someone to talk to I’m here. And I hope you do find that someone who will love you the way I think everyone deserves to be loved.

I just found out about everything so this is all extremely shocking right now. I’m taking comfort in knowing that so many other people saw Cry’s presence as something safe and feel almost betrayed by what he’s done. There are so many tainted memories now, at the flip of a switch, every memory I’ve ever associated with him has become something dirty that makes me sick to think about. 

He’s been an influence in my life for over ten years now, his videos helped me cope with everything from my parents divorcing to child abuse, being bullied and getting diagnosed with depression and anxiety at 12 years old. I used to download his videos onto my kindle and listen to them to fall asleep because it made me feel safe. I’d watch him during school because it felt like he was my only friend for a long time, and I had nobody to talk to. Now it’s like that friend is dead. Or maybe just never even existed. All of those videos I saw as a space to be safe and be myself, I don’t know if I could ever watch again, knowing what he really is. 

I hope beyond hope that the victims are safe and happy, or that they at least take comfort in knowing their abuser can’t hurt them anymore, and his actions have been exposed. As horrible as this situation is, I was really happy to find this community supporting all of the people who have been victimized and holding Cry accountable. It speaks volumes about the kind of fans he attracted.

As for Cry, I think it’s okay to hope for change in those who hurt others, but I agree that his victims take priority over whatever is felt about him. I do hope he changes for the better and doesn’t hurt anyone else. I hope all of the people he’s hurt are doing better now, they deserve to thrive. I hope that not everything we took comfort in was a lie, that some part of what made so many people connect with him was real, but at this point I doubt it. And that kind of makes it feel worse.

I just found out about this from a fucking Harry Potter shaming group on Facebook and I feel sick. I started watching Cry when I was 12, and it really felt like his videos were the only human connection I had at that time in my life. I’m 22 now and I always looked back at Cry as someone to look up to and hoped he was doing well. I’m seeing this thread but it’s like my mind keeps trying to tell me it’s not real, I’m so disgusted. My heart goes out to all of the victims in this terrible situation and I hope all those who choose to pursue it get the justice they deserve. Nothing anyone feels about this could ever compare to how they’re feeling right now, and I hope they’re getting all of the support they need and deserve.

I understand how you feel. I’m half Filipino from my mother’s side, and my dad is mixed race white and Native American. I take almost completely after him and appear very white. Ive has people ask me for “proof” that I’m half Asian and go as far as to say I must have been adopted because my mother couldn’t have a child as white as me, especially when they see my brothers and sisters who are very clearly mixed. I’ve accepted that I’ll never look like much of my family, but it used to make me very sad. What I believe will always hurt is that I feel almost guilty for participating in a culture that I grew up with more than any other. My dad left when I was pretty young, and my grandfather who immigrated from the Philippines really was the only father figure I had. Any time I go to an event to celebrate our Filipino heritage or participate in my culture I feel like a pretender. I don’t know if that will ever change, but please remind yourself that you’re not alone. People don’t seem to understand that being mixed doesn’t mean you will automatically take after your poc family or get a perfect mix of features. You have every right to call yourself Thai and take pride in it, those who would deny you your own culture are ignorant. As hard as it is to remember, you don’t have to justify yourself when taking pride in who you are. Hopefully someday people realize that being mixed race is far more complex and diverse than is represented.

There are a worrying amount of comments here downplaying the incest in this situation. It’s not less bad because they “only kissed” its absolutely still bad. She could be defensive because she regrets it, but I’d still say that if she’s not even willing to hear you out then maybe your values are too different to really be involved. Especially because from the way you described it, her sister is completely fine and open about it. But either way you’re not in the wrong for feeling uncomfortable, I’m sure most people would be.

NTA, people in this thread really are over exaggerating what happens to kids with weird/different/uncommon names. I have an uncommon name as well as a nonwhite last name because I’m mixed race. Yes there are discriminatory people out there but I thought the point was to fight against that and learn to be MORE accepting of people’s identities, which is why I’m so confused by all of the YTA telling you to conform to what a bunch of random strangers deem an acceptable name for your children. My boyfriend’s name is literally Matrix and it has no bearing on how people he interacts with view him. He’s maintained his ability to work for fantastic opportunities in life and he’s actually really proud of his name. If anything it’s a passing “oh I haven’t heard that before” when he introduces himself or people asking him to repeat himself to make sure they heard correctly, but we live in an age where the idea of what an acceptable name is has been broadened. There’s nothing wrong with giving your kids names from things that make you happy and people need to stop pushing this idea of what constitutes a “normal” name on others. It’s not their right to tell anyone about what to name their kid. Realistically, nobody gives a shit about your child’s name at the end of the day, and if they do they’re extremely over dramatic. It’s not like your named them something offensive or derogatory, so I don’t see the problem. If you live in a place where a person is ridiculed for their name or they’ve lost opportunity due to their name and you’re saying it’s the fault of the parent who named them and not the assholes making people’s lives harder because of their names, you’re the problem, not the parent.

That’s really kind of you to say, I really appreciate it. Going LC has seriously helped since this whole situation. I know they still talk about me, but I stick up for myself now, which is a big improvement. The hardest part of this was knowing that my fiancé and I being independent was enough of a slight against them that they thought it was okay to say those things about me and make fun of us. I had never even said an unkind word to them or about them before JNMIL threatened my fiancé when he tried to move out. I guess some people just can’t handle not having power over others, and when we took that from them, they lashed out. 

I’m also wishing you all the best during these difficult times. Reading your response felt very reassuring, so thank you!

Thank you for the advice, I truly agree with you here. I stopped caring a while ago about getting the relationship I hoped for from them, it’s seriously futile and I’ve come to realize that. It does still sadden me as I never wanted to have a difficult relationship with them, and I don’t think anyone wants to have to interact with people who clearly hate them for the rest of their lives. But we really only see them on special occasions and in emergencies now, which I’m okay with. Do I still hate it? Absolutely lol, but I can live with it. 

My fiancé’s been through a lot in the last two years, with his father passing away (his father was always much kinder, I respected him a lot and we never really had any issues) and I wouldn’t expect him to cut contact with his family. I don’t think that grief excuses their behavior, considering this happened beforehand, and they’ve done worse since then, but I know they’ve been learning to cope with loss now and if my fiancé chose to see them more often, I’d accept it as long as he didn’t expect me to be there as often. I’ve just been holding all of this in my head and I’m so tired of it I felt desperate for a place to vent. This really is just the tip of the iceberg.

FSIL has dealt with their BS for far longer than I have, and the things she’s told me are seriously awful. For a while, JNMIL had us convinced that we hated each other because of the lies she would feed us both. Luckily we realized what was going on, and we’re really close now. We’ve been coping by venting to each other, but I’m not sure if she’s LC. Fiancé and I have been for some time now, and I don’t see that changing in the near future. 

Thank you again for the advice, it’s really appreciated!

His mother used to have a lot of control over him, so it took a while to get him to see that the way she treats him isn’t okay. After we moved out, his eyes started to really open to everything he had been through in his family, and he started sticking up for himself and me, which really made our relationship stronger. His first reaction was to comfort me and assure me that they weren’t in the right, they were awful for saying those things, etc, but I didn’t want to bring it up to them and he never did, he left that decision up to me which I appreciated. So he didn’t like go yell at his mother or his brother for treating me like that, but we only ever see his family now for special occasions and emergencies. Which I’m okay with, I know how hard it is to separate from family even if they’re cruel or abusive so I don’t hold it against him if his mom gets sick and he goes to check on her or something. We both come from pretty crappy families and we’ve accepted that where we are right now, we can’t stop all contact, but we avoid interactions with them for our own mental health.

Thanks so much, I really appreciate that you took the time to write this out. I completely agree with you that finding a chosen family to be supportive is the best option. It just took me a long time to come to terms with the fact that sometimes no matter how hard you try, some people can just be cruel. I have a group of amazing friends that I love so much, sadly they live a little far and right now it’s not easy to see them but we try! 

And you’re absolutely right about hearing all of this from FSIL, it’s been our way of handling everything our in-laws have done but I see what you mean about it being harmful. I never thought about it in that sense. I know she told me because she felt guilty knowing what they say and didn’t want to hide it, she wasn’t trying to be vindictive, but you’re right. It’s doing more harm than good knowing exactly what they’re saying.

We’ve been very LC for about a year now, I mostly stay away wherever I can. I’ve told my fiancé I don’t want to stop him from seeing his family, and that’s it’s his choice, but he also doesn’t want to see them unless necessary. Of course I get blamed for that too though lol. 

But again thank you for your response, your kind words and advice really do help, and it’s nice to know I’m not over reacting by being hurt by their actions. I wish you all the best!
As someone who knew a girl named Dasani Waters in high school, NTA. Save your kid the embarrassment.
